granted is a team of technologists and problem-solvers who value clear thinking and careful execution. We focus on building something functional, well-considered, and genuinely useful in the time we have.
summary: At the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we tackled the MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspot harmonization problem. The two NASA sensors detect fires at different resolutions and sensitivities, so their records cannot be compared directly. Our solution is a web app that produces one consistent Burning Activity Calendar. Users draw an area of interest on a 2D map. The app retrieves NASA FIRMS hotspots from both sensors, harmonizes them with our pre-trained AI Rapid Harmonization Engine, and displays historical fire activity as an accessible color-coded calendar with downloadable data. The engine learns sensor relationships from the FIRMS archive, so users see fire patterns and anomalies rather than sensor differences. The workflow targets a region in under five minutes versus over an hour manually, and it requires no coding. Fire managers, scientists, and land managers gain one clearer picture for historical comparison and monitoring. Next steps include real-time alerts, fire-type classification, and broader regional coverage. Near-real-time prediction is a future goal, not a claim about the current prototype.
details: Burn Calendar is a web application that harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspot data into a single consistent Burning Activity Calendar. Users draw an area of interest on a 2D map. The app retrieves NASA FIRMS hotspots from both sensors, applies our pre-trained AI Rapid Harmonization Engine to remove sensor differences, and displays historical fire activity as an accessible color-coded calendar with downloadable CSV data. The engine learns relationships between the two sensor records from the FIRMS archive, so users see fire patterns and anomalies rather than sensor artifacts. Benefits include a unified view, fast processing (target under five minutes per region versus over an hour manually), and no coding required. Intended impact is better historical comparison and monitoring for fire managers, scientists, and land managers. Tools used: Python, TensorFlow for the harmonization model, React and Leaflet for the front end, and the NASA FIRMS API. The project is creative in replacing manual cross-sensor calibration with a learned model and in presenting results as an intuitive calendar. We considered accessibility with color ramps, simplicity for non-technical users, and honesty about current capabilities (near-real-time prediction is a future goal, not a current feature).
